title: Harbor and Compass
premise: In the waning months of the Republic of Vessany, Dominic Underhill carries sealed diplomatic codes between ministries, convinced he is a bystander to history. When a census taker's probing question exposes him as the unwitting courier of documents proving the government ordered a massacre, Dominic must choose between safe silence and smuggling the evidence through three military checkpoints to a foreign press. Betrayed by his handler and sheltered by a ragtag family of smugglers who claim him as their own, he reaches the harbor at last — but only by surrendering the codes that were his identity. The truth prints; the republic falls anyway; and Dominic, stateless but no longer alone, learns that belonging is something you carry, not something you're issued.
about_author: Bram Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the papers of collapsed governments. Harbor and Compass is their first novel, drawn from the marginalia of documents that almost didn't survive.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A routine census interview in the capital unravels when the taker asks about the contents of his satchel — questions no census asks. Fleeing, Dominic discovers his diplomatic codes conceal massacre orders meant for destruction. He seeks out his handler, Ilse, who vanishes rather than help. Emotional beat: the shattering of a man's comfortable belief that history happens elsewhere.

chapters.title: The Salt Road Family
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with interludes from smuggler captain Maren Oduya. Hunted after Ilse names him to authorities, Dominic is taken in by Maren's crew of outcasts — a forger, a defrocked priest, a boy who reads tide charts like scripture. They agree to move him and the evidence to the coastal city of Bral. Emotional beat: wary strangers becoming, without ceremony, a family.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Dominic and Maren. The journey becomes a gauntlet: a forged pass fails at the river checkpoint, forcing the priest to sacrifice his freedom as a decoy; the second checkpoint nearly breaks them when the boy is detained. At the third, Dominic learns Ilse has been arrested and could exonerate him — if he abandons the mission. Emotional beat: rising dread and the cost of each choice measured in people.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Maren's POV closing into Dominic's. At Bral's harbor, soldiers seal the docks; Maren's ship is boarded and the satchel seized. But Dominic has already memorized and re-copied the evidence, hidden in the boy's tide charts, and it reaches the foreign press as the republic collapses. Ilse escapes in the chaos; the found family scatters, then regathers on Maren's deck. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging — home as the people who stayed.
